texts.orig: The sample-size calculation assumption was developed based on the results from the DEFUSE 3 and EXTEND-IA TNK trials. With this assumption, we estimated that 456 patients, after accounting for a 5% dropout rate, would provide at least 90% power to detect the difference of a shift towards improvement (ie, a lower score) in the 90-day modified Rankin Scale between the two treatment arms at a two-sided 0.049 significance level, after adjusting for one interim efficacy analysis. Type I error levels were determined according to the Lan-DeMets theory for alpha-spending function that approximates the O'Brien-Fleming boundary.

texts.orig: Two safety-only interim analyses were planned and conducted when the first 25 and 50 patients had completed the 72-to-96-hours visit assessment after randomization. Additionally, per request from the independent data monitoring committee, two safety data reviews were later added that were planned to occur when the first 100 and 200 patients had completed the 72-to-96-hours visit assessment after randomization. Nonbinding sequential boundaries were used to monitor the symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) rate at those interim safety reviews in order to halt the trial if an excessive number of sICH cases was observed.

texts.orig: In Figure 2, age subgroups were adjusted for protocol version (1-4 vs 5) and baseline NIHSS (≤15 vs >15); the subgroup with age <80 years was additionally adjusted for type of occlusion (ICA/M1 vs M2). NIHSS subgroups were adjusted for protocol version (1-4 vs 5) and ag e (≤70 vs >70 years); the NIHSS ≤15 subgroup was additionally adjusted for type of occlusion (ICA/M1 vs M2). Subgroups for time between stroke onset to randomization were adjusted for protocol version (1-4 vs 5) and type of occlusion (ICA/M1 vs M2); additionally, the subgroup that had <16 hours between stroke onset to randomization was adjusted for age (≤70 vs >70 years). Subgroups for planned EVT (planned or not planned) were adjusted for protocol version (14 vs 5); additionally, the subgroup with planned EVT was also adjusted for type of occlusion (ICA/M1 vs M2) and age (≤70 vs >70 years). Both subgroups for performed EVT (performed or not performed) were adjusted for protocol version (14 vs 5); additionally, the subgroup that underwent EVT was also adjusted for age (≤70 vs >70 years) and baseline NIHSS (≤15 vs >15). For the subgroup for which EVT was not performed, the model was also adjusted for EVT planned (yes vs no). All three subgroups for elapsed time between trial drug administration and groin puncture were adjusted for protocol version (14 vs 5); additionally, the ≤6 minutes subgroup was also adjusted for baseline NIHSS (≤15 vs >15), and the >6 to ≤22 minutes and >22 minutes subgroups were also adjusted for age (≤70 vs >70 years). All three subgroups for baseline infarct volume were adjusted for age (≤70 vs >70 years); additionally, the subgroups with baseline infarct volume <20 mL and ≥ 20 mL to <50 mL were also adjusted for protocol version (1 -4 vs 5). The subgroup with baseline infarct volume <20 mL was also adjusted for type of occlusion (ICA/M1 vs M2). Each occlusion subgroup was adjusted for age (≤70 vs >70 years); additionally, the M1 and M2 subgroups were also adjusted for protocol version (1-4 vs 5), and the M1 subgroup was also adjusted for baseline NIHSS (≤15 vs >15).

All three subgroups for baseline infarct volume were adjusted for age (≤70 vs >70 years); additionally, the subgroups with baseline infarct volume <20 mL and ≥ 20 mL to <50 mL were also adjusted for protocol version (1 -4 vs 5). texts.orig: Hypothesis testing of the secondary efficacy outcomes would be performed only if the primary efficacy analysis was statistically significant. To account for multiplicity, tests of the secondary outcomes were to be conducted sequentially, as detailed in the main text above and in study Statistical Analysis Plan, until a negative result indicated by a P value >0.049. P values were not provided for any subsequent analyses of the secondary outcomes following a negative test and the 95% CIs should not be used for hypothesis testing.
